newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Faulding to open Medicine Shoppes.
newsitem.headline: Faulding to open Medicine Shoppes.

text.p: Drug maker and distributor F.H. Faulding and Co Ltd said it would expand its domestic retail pharmacy operations with a deal to open 100 Medicine Shoppe stores over the next five years.
Faulding Healthcare division chief operating officer David Murphy said the company would pay a royalty to the Medicine Shoppe group's parent company Cardinal Health Inc.
Murphy would not disclose the amount to be paid.
He said the company's decision to increase its retail presence in Australia, where individual pharmacies are owned by registered chemists, would cost A$30 million over five years.

This expenditure would include the cost of starting up the Medicine Shoppe franchise concept, which was focussed on prescription-based delivery located near hospitals and medical centres, and the expansion of the Chem-Mart retail unit which now had 350 stores.

Murphy said Faulding expected to have 1,000 stores in five years. The company would have a four-pronged retail strategy in the near future, he said, with the other two areas to be announced on August 6 during a national teleconference hook-up with pharmacists.

The introduction of Medicine Shoppe operations in Australia would improve Faulding's profitability, he said without providing specific figures, by increasing retail margins and allowing for better use of stock.
